title: The S8 context pack and the S8 module extracts are absent from the workspace
source: WP B2-S8-008 read-only list (_work/msr/context/S8.md and _work/msr/extract/ files whose name contains S8); knowledge of the workspace root
description: The work package names a context pack and a set of module extracts as the authority for service facts, the ownership rows, the matching slides and the naming rules, and neither the context folder nor the extract folder exists in this workspace. The service row, the ownership rows of deviation, recovery_case, timer, decision_log_entry and rule_row, the connection matrix row S8 and the slide references are therefore taken from Template and Rules v1 R4, FSD S8 v3 and TSD S8 v2, which state the naming rule, the table owners and the cross-module interfaces but not the slide-level call types.
evidence: _work/msr contains only assumptions, editlog, fragments, gaps and smoke; the only earlier output is B2-S2-015, which records the same absence as CG-B2-S2-015-9
proposed: Issue the S8 context pack with the service row, the five ownership rows and the connection matrix row, and re-check section 12 of both stories against it; the naming, the ownership and the boundaries already agree with Template and Rules R4, TSD S8 T3.3 and T5.2

title: No route rule and no requirement row names FEAT-DVF-08
source: FSD S8 v3 A2.17.3.1; TSD S8 v2 T8; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 route set Deviations
description: The FSD gives FEAT-DVF-08 Review an override two validation rules, VR-S8-017-1 and BR-S8-017, and no R-DEV row, while every other feature of the module carries at least one. TSD S8 T8 maps REQ-DVH-001 to REQ-DVH-011 and REQ-S8-001 to REQ-S8-007 to FEAT-DVH-01 and FEAT-DVF-01, and no row names FEAT-DVF-08, so the story has no requirement ID to cite. The outcome the forum records therefore has to be read against the outcome rows that do exist, R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-11 and R-DEV-22.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.17.3.1 table of two rules; TSD S8 T8 rows REQ-DVH-001 to REQ-S8-007; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22
proposed: Add one R-DEV row for the review that fires on the recorded outcome, and one REQ row for FEAT-DVF-08, in the next issue of the FSD and the TSD; until then the story cites no REQ ID and selects one of the four outcome rows

title: The mapping from the outcome list to the DEVIATION to-states is not published
source: TSD S8 v2 T3.2 and T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 route set Deviations; FSD S8 v3 A2.17
description: TSD S8 T3.2 publishes LOV-DEV-OUTCOME with RETURNED, RE_ROUTED and CASE_ENDED, and T4 publishes nine states over 22 rules, but no source states which value drives which row. The four rows that can fire on a recorded outcome are R-DEV-09 (to DEV_RESOLVED, codes X1 and X7), R-DEV-10 (to DEV_REROUTE, code X2), R-DEV-11 (to CASE_ENDED, insurance settled) and R-DEV-22 (to DEV_REROUTE, an outcome that names no next step). The story records the mapping it applies and does not treat it as a published value.
evidence: TSD S8 T3.2 list LOV-DEV-OUTCOME; T4 rows R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-11 and R-DEV-22; FSD S8 A2.17.3.1 carries no rule row
proposed: Publish the mapping as a reference-data row of the DEVIATION route set and have the business lead confirm it at the baseline review; the story applies the reading written in section 9 until then

title: The review trigger, the queue read and the entitlement of the review role are not published
source: TSD S8 v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; FSD S8 v3 A2.17.3.3
description: TSD S8 T-A.1 publishes two operations, API-S8-001 raise and API-S8-002 outcome, and no operation that reads the deviation queue SCR-08 lists, and T-A.2 declares the outcome operation with right U on the case record. FSD S8 A2.17.3.3 makes the risk and model risk officer the primary role of the review, with the conduct and QA officer and the center of excellence analyst as further users, while TSD S8 T6.1 gives RW-RISK, RW-CONDUCT and RW-COE right R only. The trigger of the review, the shape of the review panel and the entitlement each role needs to record a review are therefore not stated.
evidence: TSD S8 T-A.1 two operations; T6.1 rows RW-RISK R, RW-CONDUCT R, RW-COE R; FSD S8 A2.17.3.3
proposed: Publish the queue read on the deviation base and settle the right the review role holds, then replace the placeholders of section 12.1 and section 10; the operation keeps right U as T-A.1 declares it

title: No source states whether the review clears the deviation or publishes DeviationCleared
source: FSD S8 v3 A2.6 and A2.17; TSD S8 v2 T3.1, T5.3; legacy RWB-E7-008 feature FEAT-DVF-08
description: The deviation row carries cleared_at (DF-CAS-044), the contact stop (DF-CAS-043) and the paused state (DF-CAS-041), and TSD S8 T5.3 publishes DeviationCleared. FEAT-DVH-06 Clear a deviation and resume the timers records the outcome, lifts the stop and resumes the clock with R-DEV-07, R-DEV-08 and R-DEV-18, and FEAT-DVF-08 records the outcome of the review without saying whether the deviation is cleared by it. The two features overlap on the outcome field and on the stop.
evidence: TSD S8 T3.1 DF-CAS-041, DF-CAS-043 and DF-CAS-044; T5.3 DeviationCleared; FSD S8 A2.6 and A2.17
proposed: Keep the clearance with FEAT-DVH-06 as the story states, and add one sentence to both features in the next FSD issue that names which of them sets cleared_at and which publishes DeviationCleared

title: The operation names and shapes of the three consumed rows are not published
source: TSD S8 v2 T5.2 and T6.1; RWB-P3-E1007-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON; legacy RWB-E7-008 section 12
description: TSD S8 T5.2 states that calls go through the published interfaces of P3 for the case and P7 for the decision log, and T6.2 declares the access rules, but neither document states the path, the query, the answer shape or the error text of the case read, of the case-move answer or of the package read. The three rows are consumed by the review and the plan's C row is None.
evidence: TSD S8 T5.2 paragraph and T6.2; T-A.1 carries no read operation; legacy section 12 carries no consumed operation
proposed: Read all three answers through the published contracts of rwb-case and rwb-decision and take the concrete paths from API Specification v5 when the files are issued; the rows carry the placeholder until then

title: The pattern set omits DP-04, DP-09 and DP-10 and the C row is None while three contracts are consumed
source: WP B2-S8-008 story lines (patterns DP03, DP13, DP19; C empty); FSD S8 v3 A2.17 and A2.2; TSD S8 v2 T2, T4 and T5.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5
description: The plan fixes three patterns for this key, while the module evaluates a rule package (DP-04), owns a topic that carries two published events (DP-09) and uses Quartz for the stage clock and the clearance (DP-10), and the story consumes three contracts although the C row is empty. The metadata H and C rows are copied from the work package as fixed, and the story declares what it builds against on Day 1 and what it does not.
evidence: WP line for RWB-S8-E7008-APP: patterns DP03, DP13, DP19, C empty; FSD S8 A2.2 integration points Workbench and Quartz scheduler; TSD S8 T5.3 two published events
proposed: Record DP-04, DP-09 and DP-10 on the steps that need them (the raise, pause and clearance stories) and the three consumed rows as class C in the plan; this story keeps the fixed rows and states the difference in section 13
